notes: Two executables now: an installer and an uninstaller, each carrying everything it needs -- HSBG, AutoHotkey v2, the plugin loader and a matching unstripped corlib -- so nothing is downloaded during a install. The installer finds Hearthstone, moves any other speed mod aside rather than deleting it, points the loader at the corlib it just unpacked, builds the speed plugin against the game actually on the machine, and shows a page at the end saying what it did and where each piece went. The uninstaller is the more important of the two: HSBG writes files outside its own folder, so deleting the folder is not an uninstall, and the plugin would keep loading into Hearthstone on every launch afterwards. Desktop shortcuts no longer target the .ahk file. Text editors register themselves as the handler for that extension -- Notepad++ writes an ahk_auto_file ProgId and wins the association even when AutoHotkey's own registration is intact -- so a shortcut that pointed at the script opened HSBG as a text document instead of running it. Both shortcuts now name AutoHotkey directly and pass the script as an argument, which takes the association out of the question entirely. The plugin loader's console window is switched off: this build of the loader defaults it on and writes its configuration file on first run, so a fresh install looked clean and a black console appeared over the game at the first launch. The in-game overlay was rebuilt as a column on the left edge. The cog is gone and so is the skip button -- the readouts are readouts, and a control that changes the game no longer sits where the eye goes to read the current state. MENU opens the settings window directly, and a key legend underneath explains what each hotkey does and can be clicked to press it, except the one that closes the session. The settings window is one page instead of five tabs, in two columns, larger, and it opens on the monitor the session is locked to rather than wherever Windows puts it. Speeds are no longer limited to the presets in the configuration file: a slider walks the presets and the box beside it takes any number typed into it. Resizing shares the extra width between the two columns and repaints once per gesture instead of once per control. Phase detection reads Hearthstone's own Power.log, so combat gets one speed and everything else another, F5 to F8 retune whichever is in force, and automatic combat skipping on F9 presses F1 rather than implementing a second, weaker skip.
